title: Two-phase commit (one round, staggered votes)
source: Own model of textbook two-phase commit: one coordinator, N participants, one round, no crashes and no timeouts (the file cites no paper). The stagger unit delta and the bounds L = 0, U = 1, sd = 0 are ours.
property: A participant that receives Commit must have voted Yes (std assert!(yes) in the participant, line 137).
citable_note: The timed mode runs a different program: only there participant i sleeps (i + 1) * delta before voting and the coordinator sleeps delta before each vote receive (lines 120-125 and 89-93), which builds by hand the vote order that the clock is then credited with removing (2^N * N! complete executions down to 2^N). The 2026-09-18 audit verdict (not citable) holds on the current source; in addition the assertion cannot fail in this model.
config_timed: build_config, line 149: Config::builder().with_all_sends_lossy().with_timed(0, 1, 0), so L = 0, U = 1, sd = 0, fixed in the source (no flag). Tool defaults for the rest (lib.rs, ConfigBuilder::new, lines 347-383): consistency model FIFO, scheduling policy LTR, keep-going off, sequential (the binary has no parallel option). Every send may be dropped, without a budget. Every receive is blocking (recv_msg_block_timed, lines 77, 94, 115, 135): the protocol has no timeout. delta = --delta; the source requires delta >= 2 (lines 267-270).
config_baseline: build_config, line 145: Config::builder().with_all_sends_lossy().build(): FIFO, LTR, keep-going off, sequential; every send may be dropped, without a budget. No clock. --delta is parsed and checked but has no effect in this mode.
program_differs_between_modes: yes: two timed-only sleeps in the protocol code. (1) coordinator, lines 89-93: if mode == Mode::Timed, traceforge::sleep(delta) before each of the N vote receives. (2) participant, lines 120-125: if mode == Mode::Timed, traceforge::sleep(delta * (index + 1)) before the vote is chosen and sent. Both functions take the mode as a parameter (lines 76 and 114). The source comment at lines 90-91 gives the purpose: stagger the receive windows so that only one participant's vote is consistent with each receive.
failing_tasks: Participant threads only: std assert!(yes) at line 137. A failure would be a Rust panic in that thread and exit code 101. It is not a traceforge::assert, so keep-going could not count it (lib.rs, lines 463-465) and no task-N line would be printed; whether such a panic is checked against the timeline in timed mode was not examined. The coordinator and the main thread assert nothing. It never fired.

counters.meaning: COMMITS (line 103): explored executions, complete or blocked, in which the coordinator decided Commit. Measured: 2^N on the timed side (64, 128) and 2^N * N! on the baseline (46080; 645120 in v8), that is the one all-Yes vote vector times the 2^N loss patterns of the N decision messages (times the N! vote arrival orders in the baseline). It equals execs only by coincidence of the two formulas. Not a violation count.

ABORTS (line 106): explored executions, complete or blocked, in which the coordinator decided Abort: (2^N - 1) vote vectors times 2^N loss patterns (times N! in the baseline), for example 63 * 64 = 4032 at N=6 timed. It exceeds execs. Not a violation count.

param_columns.meaning: number of participants (--participants); one coordinator in addition
stagger unit (--delta): participant i (from 0) sleeps (i + 1) * delta before it votes and the coordinator sleeps delta before each vote receive; timed side only
transit lower bound, fixed 0 in the source; timed side only
transit upper bound, fixed 1 in the source; timed side only
storage delay, fixed 0 in the source; timed side only

regimes.name: staggered votes
regimes.params: L=0, U=1, sd=0, delta=5 (timed side only: participant i, counted from 0, sleeps (i + 1) * 5 ticks before it votes; the coordinator sleeps 5 ticks before each vote receive)
regimes.rule: No timing boundary: the assertion holds with and without the clock. Control for the verdict only (the two sides must agree on 0 violations). With delta >= 2 the sleeps leave one possible sender for each vote receive (file header, lines 19-32), so the N! arrival orders of the baseline collapse to one, as the measured 2^N complete executions confirm; this comes from sleeps that only the timed program contains, so the two counts do not measure what the clock removes from one program.

glossary.meaning: the coordinator asks every participant for its vote
each participant chooses its vote nondeterministically (traceforge::nondet(), line 127) and sends it once: 2^N vote vectors
the coordinator reads N votes with blocking receives and sends Commit to all if all N are Yes, else Abort
timed side only: sleeps that spread the votes and the vote receives delta ticks apart. They are part of the timed program only, which is why the comparison is not citable.
complete executions of the timed side (one per vote vector) and of the baseline (vote vectors times the arrival orders of the N votes at the coordinator)
explored executions (complete or blocked) in which the coordinator decided Commit or Abort; they are not violation counts

a thread waits forever on a blocking receive because the message it needs was dropped. With every send lossy and no timeout in the protocol this is almost all of the explored executions (timed N=6: 79722 blocked, 64 complete).

notes: Not citable. Audit of 2026-09-18 checked against the current source: it names lines 89 and 123; the two timed-only blocks are now at lines 89-93 (coordinator) and 120-125 (participant), the sleeps themselves at lines 92 and 124. The standing rule (memory note three_pc_delta_commit_feasibility, 2026-07-05) forbids mode-conditional sleeps in a benchmark that compares the two modes; this example breaks it by design, as its header (lines 13-32) describes.

The older memory note feedback_raft_temporal_framing describes the 2PC stagger as a reduction on the same protocol. The rule of 2026-07-05 and the audit come later and decide the matter: the sleeps exist only in the timed program.

The assertion cannot fail here: every participant sends exactly one vote and the coordinator commits only after reading N Yes votes, so a Commit implies that the receiving participant voted Yes. The binary has no switch that breaks the rule, so nothing shows the assertion failing.

The header's claim, total exploration shrinks from 2^N * N! to 2^N, is about complete executions. With every send lossy the explored counts are dominated by blocked executions: 79786 against 3109366 at N=6 (39 times), 546042 against 84820978 at N=7 (155 times, baseline from v8).

Counters: the compare output of the binary labels commit and abort "(complete execs)" (line 220); that label is wrong, they include blocked executions (abort=4032 with execs=64 at N=6 timed). commit + abort = 2^N * 2^N on the timed side (4096 at N=6, 16384 at N=7): every vote vector times every loss pattern of the N decision messages.

The counters are not in the counters column of results_v9.csv: the plan's counters_spec has no pattern for commit or abort, so that column is empty for this example. They are only in the summary column.

The summary line prints only the number of participants (line 179): delta, L, U and sd do not appear in it. They are resolved from the arguments (--delta 5) and from the source (with_timed(0, 1, 0), line 149). There are no ratio flags.
violation_counter is null: no summary counter counts violations. The violating-execution count 0 comes from the exit code.

kind: the binary has no keep-going option (ConfigBuilder default, lib.rs line 353), so every cell is first-violation by the rule of FORMAT.md; all finished runs exit with code 0, which means that no violation exists and the whole space was explored.
No v9 result on 2026-10-11 for the N=7 baseline (legacy-018, two runs planned); its entry uses v8.
Wall time, N=6 (medians of three v9 repetitions): timed 21 s, baseline 231 s.
Regime: one timing setting in both cells and no timing boundary, so there is one regime, S (staggered), with the suffix -ctrl (the two sides agree on 0 violations).
